title: A polynomial-time decoding algorithm up to half the square-root bound for quadratic residue and generalized quadratic residue codes
summary: Binary quadratic residue (QR) codes, introduced by Prange in 1958, are cyclic codes of prime length $p\equiv\pm1\pmod 8$ and dimension $(p+1)/2$ whose minimum distance satisfies the square-root bound $d\ge\sqrt p$. They include the Hamming code $[7,4,3]$ and the Golay code $[23,12,7]$, and were generalized by van Lint and MacWilliams to generalized quadratic residue (GQR) codes of prime-power length $q$, for which the bound $d\ge\sqrt q$ still holds and is attained when $q$ is a square. In coding theory, one usually first finds a lower bound on the minimum distance of a family of codes, and then a polynomial-time algorithm decoding up to half of this bound, as for BCH, Reed--Muller or Gabidulin codes. Until now, GQR codes had resisted this approach: no such algorithm was known, apart from individual short lengths. We give a deterministic algorithm which, for every odd prime power $q\equiv\pm1\pmod 8$, corrects every error pattern of weight at most $\lfloor(\sqrt q-1)/2\rfloor$ in the binary GQR code of length $q$, in $O(q^{9/2})$ operations in $\F_q$. We start from a description of QR codes due to Helleseth, which we extend to GQR codes, and in which the syndrome gives the values of the quadratic character of the error-locator polynomial. We then recover this polynomial by adapting to GQR codes the tools that Kopparty developed for recovering polynomials from noisy character values, with the decoding of dual BCH codes as an application. Since the square-root bound is attained when $q$ is a square, this radius is the largest that can be guaranteed uniformly on the class of GQR codes.

title: An upper bound on non-overlapping codes
summary: Non-overlapping codes (also known as bifix-free codes or strong comma-free codes) have now been studied for over 60 years as part of information theory, with regular new applications appearing and much recent interest. Let $X$ be a binary non-overlapping code of length $n$. The paper contains a self-contained proof that \[ |X|\leq \left(\frac{5}{6e} +O(n^{-1})\right)\frac{2^n}{n} \] as $n\rightarrow\infty$. This improves, by a factor of $5/6$, the best previously known bound due to Levenshtein (1970). The paper builds on work by Fimmel, Michel, Pirot, Sereni and Strüngmann (2019), and by Stanovnik, Mo\v skon and Mraz (2024).

title: Computed Permutation Trellis Coding: Near-Optimal Quantization from Two Multiplications and a 64-Byte Table
summary: We propose Computed Permutation Trellis Coding (CPTC), a low-bit quantization format for tensors written once and read many times. Formats that round each value on its own, such as INT4 and FP4, waste a large part of their bits against the information-theoretic ideal. Trellis codes recover this loss by encoding values jointly, but prior decoders either need a large lookup table for their best quality or compute values with a hash that restricts what they can decode. CPTC's decoder multiplies its state by two coefficients and adds the top bits of the products to index a 64-byte table. Because that sum is not uniformly distributed, the rarely used ends of a small table can hold values far out in the tails. One decoder serves every bit width from 1 to 6, reproduces the standard integer and floating-point formats exactly, and comes within 0.07 bits of the ideal at 4 bits. It matches a random-permutation trellis code whose table is thousands of times larger, and exceeds every QTIP codebook. In LLM weight quantization without fine-tuning, CPTC has the lowest KL divergence to the unquantized model at every tested bit width on Llama 3.1 8B and 70B Instruct against QTIP's codebooks (by up to 27%). The decoder has been built into the AWS Trainium 4 AI accelerator, where it runs at the throughput of the native FP4 and FP8 formats for a negligible fraction of the systolic array's area. Fused encoding kernels quantize an 8B model's linear layers in under two minutes on one GPU and, in cycle-level simulation, on one Trainium 4 chip.

title: Subsystem Stabilizer $(r,δ)$-Locally Recoverable Codes: Characterization, Bounds and Constructions
summary: Local erasure recovery limits the number of physical systems accessed to repair a distributed quantum memory. For subsystem stabilizer codes (SSCs), a basic question is whether erasures can be corrected within a prescribed repair set. In this paper, we study subsystem stabilizer $(r,δ)$-locally recoverable codes ($(r,δ)$-SSLRCs), in which each coordinate belongs to a repair set of size between $δ$ and $r+δ-1$ that corrects any set of up to $δ-1$ erasures while preserving the logical subsystem and allowing the gauge subsystem to change. We first characterize local erasure recovery algebraically and apply this criterion to Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) and Hermitian hull constructions for $(r,δ)$-SSLRCs. For $(r,δ)$-SSLRCs, without assuming purity, we derive a redundancy bound for disjoint repair sets, a supported-subspace bound based on supported stabilizer and gauge subspaces, and a mixed counting bound for known erasures within selected repair sets and errors at unknown positions outside their union. For pure $(r,δ)$-SSLRCs with overlapping repair sets, we establish the Singleton-type and alphabet-dependent bounds, together with explicit Griesmer, Hamming, and Plotkin bounds. Moreover, we construct nine classes of $\F_q$-linear pure $(r,δ)$-SSLRCs from maximum distance separable (MDS) stabilizer codes, Reed-Solomon (RS) codes, and linear codes with MDS Hermitian hulls, which are simultaneously optimal with respect to several bounds for $(r,δ)$-SSLRCs.

title: ASCEND: Automated Shockproof Cost-Efficient Network Design
comment: Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
summary: Designing resilient and cost-effective IP network topologies over an existing physical infrastructure is a challenging combinatorial optimization problem, particularly at large scale and under extensive failure modeling assumptions. Traditional deterministic approaches struggle to jointly address resiliency against shock (large customer-impact outages) and implementation cost objectives when the number of candidate circuits grows quadratically with the number of sites to be interconnected. In this paper, we propose Automated Shockproof Cost-Efficient Network Design (ASCEND), a systematic design pipeline for IP core network optimization based on a two-level optimization framework. At the outer level, ASCEND uses Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO) to select core sites and core circuits. Given a core design, the inner-level integral Multi-Commodity Flow (MCF) formulation selects edge circuits and maps both core and edge circuits onto optical (fiber/transport) paths while prioritizing resource disjointness and latency. Network designs are evaluated using two competing objectives: a performance cost capturing resiliency under probabilistic failure scenarios and an implementation cost. The performance cost incorporates an exponentially weighted vulnerability metric that explicitly penalizes infeasible configurations. Experimental results on multiple real-world networks demonstrate that ASCEND consistently identifies designs that outperform a manually engineered baseline in both resiliency and implementation cost.

title: Beyond Reconstruction: A Unified Framework for Trustworthy and Explainable EEG Artifact Removal Evaluation
summary: Deep-learning methods have achieved strong performance in EEG artifact removal, but evaluation remains dominated by reconstruction metrics such as error, correlation, and signal-to-noise ratio. Although these metrics assess similarity to clean EEG, they do not establish whether models effectively suppress artifacts, preserve neural activity, or provide reliable explanations. To address these limitations, we propose TriX-EEG, a three-level framework for trustworthy and explainable EEG artifact removal. Level 1, Signal Validity (SV), evaluates reconstruction quality and neural band-power preservation. Level 2, Removal Faithfulness (RF), assesses the removed component through artifact error and residual artifact/neural leakage. Level 3, Explanation Reliability (ER), examines model behavior through temporal alignment, causal relevance, and stability. We evaluate TriX-EEG using nine published neural denoisers across three public benchmarks derived from EEGDenoiseNet and the PhysioNet Motion Artifact Contaminated EEG Dataset, covering EOG, EMG, and motion artifacts. Results show that reconstruction metrics alone are insufficient for trustworthy denoiser assessment: RF complements it by revealing whether errors stem from residual artifact or suppressed neural activity, while ER captures distinct aspects of explanation behavior, supporting joint evaluation of three aspects within a unified framework rather than reliance on any single factor. External validation on an independent EEG/EOG dataset and the BCI Competition IV-2a motor-imagery dataset further demonstrates broadly consistent rankings under dataset shift. Higher-ranked denoisers generally preserve more task-relevant information or cause less downstream performance degradation. Overall, TriX-EEG provides a comprehensive basis for EEG denoiser assessment, encouraging models that are not only accurate but also faithful and explainable.

title: A Critical Appraisal and Motivated Intruder Test of A Search Dataset Anonymised for the Purposes of the EU Digital Markets Act
summary:
This study evaluated the European Commission's anonymisation measures for Alphabet's search-data sharing under Article 6(11) of the Digital Markets Act against European Data Protection Board guidance and contemporary practice, and assessed re-identification through motivated intruder testing.
  The measures focus on search end-users, leaving other individuals mentioned in queries insufficiently protected, and do not explicitly address inference. The accompanying controls and safeguards reflect good practice for managing residual risk.
  Motivated intruder testing targeted 98,501 individuals across six countries using publicly available profiles. Google-verified matches yielded a re-identification rate of 0.094%, below the study's 0.47% per-team threshold. Each verified match required about three hours (Euro 105), excluding Google verification and Gemini costs, suggesting limited cost deterrence. All country-level rates were below the threshold, but one region exceeded it. The threshold drew on conservative precedents, adjusted for data quality, verification, controls and safeguards, assuming five independent attack teams.
  Some sensitivity scenarios exceeded the threshold, but relied on strong assumptions, such as treating all uncertain matches as correct. Results may not generalise beyond the targeted population, and ethics requirements constrained the attacks. Personal data detection recall was assumed rather than tested: the minimum defensible recall was 0.88, with 0.976 recommended. However, missed identifiers outside the allow-list would remain in the dataset.
  Under the study's contextual framework, assumptions and testing limitations, identity-disclosure risk was considered insignificant. This finding does not resolve the gaps concerning inference and other individuals' information; safeguards remain necessary.

title: DeltaHarness: Self-Evolving Harnesses for Resource-Adaptive Tool Execution
summary: Tool-using agents rely on execution harnesses to organize and schedule tool operations. The same task and resource description can conceal runtime conditions that reverse the latency ordering of valid execution plans. Resolving this uncertainty requires firsthand execution in the target setting. We introduce DeltaHarness, an execution-guided policy-search method that adapts agent harnesses from cold-start measurements. Its QHI loop uses the observed response to update runtime dispatch, revise physical plans, and select experiments for later proposals. An independent confirmation panel controls policy replacement. With fixed dispatch, a revised materialization policy reduces complete-delivery latency by 30.0% on one video-editing task across three fresh pairs. On held-out tasks, the evolved policies reduce latency by 8.2% relative to the best fixed plan in one seed and by 4.6% relative to the initial proposal in another.

title: The Impact of Scenario Representation in Scenario-based Optimization Certification
summary: Scenario-based optimization provides finite-sample guarantees for decisions constructed from sampled uncertainty, but its certification procedures can be sensitive to how those samples are represented. We investigate this sensitivity under lossless scenario regrouping, which preserves the sampled information, feasible region, optimizer, and primitive violation probability. For an equal-allocation support-subsample certificate, we derive the distortion factor \(k^2(1-ε)^{k-1}\), establish certification reversals between equivalent representations, and provide sufficient conditions for acceptance dominance under nested coarsening. We further apply nondegeneracy-free Wait-and-Judge theory to coordinatewise scenario envelopes, enabling stronger certification directly from the primitive observations. In paired scenario-MPC experiments, exact regrouping increases certification availability from 318 to 471 of 480 attempts without changing the samples, numerical proposals, or requiring any reduction in witness cardinality. Primitive Wait-and-Judge certification accepts the same 471 attempts without regrouping. These results demonstrate that apparent scenario sample-efficiency gains can arise from certificate accounting rather than additional information or reduced decision risk.

title: Noise Characterization and Robust Signal Detection in Yeast Pheromone Molecular Communication
summary: A critical aspect of Molecular Communications (MC) is the implementation of signal detection policies amidst noise. To date, noise characterizations within the MC field have predominantly drawn from methodologies found in wireless communications literature. In this study, we diverge from existing MC research by utilizing a newly developed experimental platform that employs yeast, allowing us to consider more realistic noise characterizations based on the relevant signaling pathways. We propose suitable signal detection mechanisms tailored to this experimental setup, which focuses on yeast cell-to-cell communications. Our analysis identifies gene transcription as the primary source of noise, and we utilize a Markov birth-death process model with Poisson arrivals and departures to characterize it. The noisy expression of the FUS1 gene is best represented using a mixed Gaussian distribution model. This model serves as a foundation for evaluating the performance of Maximum Likelihood Detection mechanisms in terms of Bit Error Rate (BER) for both symbol-by-symbol and sequence transmission schemes. Error analysis indicates that appropriate adjustments to the signal threshold can reduce errors to as low as 10%, which is not negligible. In contrast, the detection of symbol sequences demonstrates enhanced error performance, achieving error rates as low as 0.4%, albeit at the cost of increased computational complexity.

title: V2V Communications Using Blockchain-Enabled 6G Technology and Federated Learning
summary: This study proposes an interesting approach for vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication, which integrates blockchain technology, federated learning (FL), and allocation optimization of latency and resources. The research evaluates the proposed system using various performance metrics such as packet delivery ratio (PDR), model accuracy, and latency and demonstrates its superiority over existing techniques. Furthermore, the system provides enhanced security through consensus optimization and k-anonymity for data privacy. Overall, the proposed system is a promising solution for efficient and secure V2V communication in the era of connected and autonomous vehicles. Moreover, the proposed approach achieves higher reliability, lower latency, and better resource utilization compared to traditional 5G.

title: Semantic Communication via Analog RF Computing: When the Radio Computes the Meaning
summary: Semantic communication (SC) systems transmit continuous latent representations of meaning, but computing the semantic encoder at resource-constrained edge devices incurs substantial energy and memory costs. To address this challenge, we propose an end-to-end SC framework that executes the semantic encoder in the client's RF receiver front end using analog RF computing. A base station (BS) broadcasts encoder weights as RF waveforms, while each edge device reuses its receiver's passive mixer to compute semantic latents at ultra-low energy. These latents are transmitted over the uplink for network-side task inference. We show that analog computing noise across encoder layers and channel noise affecting transmitted latents admit a unified mathematical model. We define a task-posterior semantic distortion metric and derive its second-order decomposition into per-client, per-stage semantic sensitivities. Using this decomposition, we obtain a closed-form semantic-aware water-filling allocation of the total client energy budget across clients, encoder layers, and uplinks, assigning tighter accuracy targets to semantically sensitive stages. This allocation induces a broadcast beamforming problem that accounts for client-specific, per-layer accuracy requirements. We further refine the allocation through stochastic optimization and jointly design it with multi-task noise-aware training of the shared semantic model. MNIST simulations show that, at matched total client energy, the proposed allocation reduces network semantic distortion by 9.2\%-19.2\% compared with uniform precision and 5.1\%-13.1\% compared with client-blind allocation. Noise-aware co-design yields a further 46\% reduction.

AI.tldr: 利用模拟RF计算在边缘设备上执行语义编码，结合统一噪声建模、语义感知水分配和随机优化，实现能耗下语义失真显著降低。
AI.motivation: 在资源受限的边缘设备上计算语义编码器会带来巨大的能耗和存储压力，需要一种低功耗的实现方案以支持实际部署。
AI.method: 本文提出整机端SC框架，在基站广播编码器权重波形的同时，利用接收机被动混频器进行模拟语义编码，实现低能耗语义映射；对解码噪声和信道噪声统一建模，定义任务后验语义失真度量，推导其二阶分解并得到基于水分配的语义感知能量分配；随后通过随机优化进一步精细化资源分配，并与多任务噪声感知训练协同设计共享语义模型。
AI.result: MNIST仿真表明，在相同总能耗条件下，精细化分配能将网络语义失真降低9.2%-19.2%（相较于均匀精度）和5.1%-13.1%（相较于客户无差别分配），噪声感知协同设计再进一步降低46%。
AI.conclusion: 通过在边缘设备RF接收机前端实现模拟RF计算，从而在严格的能量预算下显著降低语义通信的整体语义失真。

title: Stop Early, Stay Simple: Evidence Acquisition for Power System Fault and Attack Diagnosis
summary: Diagnostic models for cyber-physical power systems usually inspect every telemetry source for every event, although some events are clear from one source and others need several. We ask when a learned policy for choosing that evidence is worth its added complexity. To answer this, we present ActiGrid, a benchmark framework for active evidence acquisition that pairs a classifier trained to tolerate missing modalities with a Double Deep Q-Network (DQN), which either requests another source or stops and diagnoses but never operates grid actuators. On the public TU Delft digital substation and MSU/ORNL power system attack benchmarks, we compare the DQN with fixed subsets and orders, calibrated entropy stopping, a greedy value of information rule, and tree ensembles trained per subset. The learned policy does adapt to what it observes, yet it is statistically indistinguishable from entropy stopping on TU Delft and Pareto dominated by simple controls on MSU/ORNL, while compact subset classifiers outperform it while reading fewer sources on both benchmarks. Entropy stopping run over those subset classifiers reaches the highest mean Macro-F1 on TU Delft (0.928 while reading 57% of the sources) but brings no saving over a static three source subset on MSU/ORNL, where no method exceeds 0.45 Macro-F1. Selective acquisition can pay off, but on these benchmarks it does not need a learned policy.

title: AdaFlowLite: Scalable and Non-blocking Inference on Asynchronous Mobile Data
summary:
The rise of mobile devices equipped with numerous sensors, such as LiDAR and cameras, has driven the adoption of multi-modal deep intelligence for distributed sensing tasks, such as smart cabins and driving assistance. However, the arrival time of mobile sensory data vary due to modality size and network dynamics, which can lead to delays (if waiting for slow data) or accuracy decline (if inference proceeds without waiting). Moreover, the diversity and dynamic nature of mobile systems exacerbate this challenge. In response, we present a shift to \textit{opportunistic} inference for asynchronous distributed multi-modal data, enabling inference as soon as partial data arrives. While existing methods focus on optimizing modality consistency and complementarity, known as modal affinity, they lack a \textit{computational} approach to control this affinity in open-world mobile environments. %
\sysname pioneers the formulation of structured cross-modality affinity in mobile contexts using a hierarchical analysis-based normalized matrix. This approach accommodates the diversity and dynamics of modalities, generalizing across different types and numbers of inputs. Employing an multi-modal lightweight Swin Transformer (MMLST), \sysname facilitates real-time and flexible data imputation, adapting to various modalities and downstream tasks without retraining. Experiments show that \sysname significantly reduces inference latency by up to 80.4\% and enhances accuracy by up to 62.1\%, while achieving nearly a 50\% reduction in energy consumption, outperforming status quo approaches. Also, this method can enhance LLM performance to preprocess asynchronous data.

title: Mechanism Design and Active Systems Theory: 60 Years of Parallel Development
summary: The survey compares two research traditions within the mathematical theory of designing the rules of interaction (mechanisms) for purposeful participants: mechanism design, together with contract theory and implementation theory, and the theory of active systems created by V.N. Burkov and developed into the theory of control in organizations (TCO) by D.A. Novikov's school; the main results of Yu.B. Germeier's school and of the domestic schools adjacent to active systems theory (AST) are covered as well. The problem statements and principal results of 2006-2026 are presented: for mechanism design (MD) - robust and dynamic mechanism design, multidimensional screening, information design, simplicity of mechanisms and credibility of the designer, market design, algorithmic and learning-based design, mechanisms for AI agents, and robust, relational, dynamic and algorithmic contracts; for AST and TCO - a general typology of control, strategy-proof and incentive-compatible planning mechanisms, decomposition of the agents' game, systems with distributed control and coalitional interaction, reflexive games and informational control, control of staff and structure, dynamic active systems, and project management. A correspondence between the classical results is established (the fair play principle and the revelation principle, the serial resource allocation mechanism and the uniform rule, active expertise mechanisms and generalized median schemes, quasi-compensatory incentive schemes and contracts under observable actions), and priorities are delineated by uniform rules; the areas where the two traditions diverge are identified, as are the dimensions of the problem (staff, structure, institutions, awareness, agents' beliefs) covered only by TCO.

title: On the Kissing Number of Craig's Lattice and Spherical List Decoding
summary: Craig's lattices $A_{p-1}^k$ are a family of lattices with large kissing numbers, i.e., relative to their dimension $n = p-1$, they contain a large number of shortest nonzero vectors. Specifically, for small $k = o(\log p / \log \log p)$, a lower bound of Bacher (2015) shows that $A_{p-1}^k$ has a super-polynomial kissing number of $ω(n^k)$. Craig's lattices are therefore attractive candidates for the construction of spherical codes. In this work, we introduce a polynomial-time list decoder for spherical codes obtained from Craig's lattices for angular distance below $45^\circ$. Our second main result shows that Bacher's lower bound is asymptotically tight for $k = o(\log p / \log \log p)$. Finally, we introduce an efficient algorithm for computing the kissing number of $A_{p-1}^k$. Using this algorithm, we compute their kissing number in dimensions up to 521. Based on this data, we pose the open question whether the kissing number of $A_{p-1}^k$ with $k \approx \sqrt{p}$ grows like $e^{Θ(\sqrt{n})}$ in dimension $n=p-1$. Concurrent work by Laarhoven and Kominers as well as Bennett, Hhan, Li and Stephens-Davidowitz proves such a bound for very closely related lattices.

title: HiGAI-Net: Hierarchical Encrypted Traffic Classification for Generative AI Services
summary: The Radio Access Network (RAN) today does not have a reliable way to identify GenAI traffic (ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, or Google Gemini traffic) at the bearer level. TLS~1.3 moves SNI into the encrypted handshake record, and Encrypted ClientHello (ECH) removes it entirely from passive inspection; Gemini has partly shifted to QUIC where SNI visibility also depends on whether ECH is deployed. Without per-flow application identity, differentiated QoS for GenAI services is not possible. HiGAI-Net tackles this using only packet-header metadata, stacking three independently trained classifiers: a binary AI/Non-AI gate (98.5 % weighted F1), a per-service resolver across ChatGPT, Copilot, and Gemini (86.4 %), and a text-vs-voice/video mode classifier (61.0 %). The core innovation is a suite of sliding-window temporal features that track how DL/UL byte-ratios evolve within a session -- the per-quarter and per-half ratio trends, a trend differential $ΔR$, and a streaming regularity index. Tested on 44,492 labeled flows, gradient-boosted tree models consistently outperformed all deep-learning variants; a per-flow label cache brings amortised inference below 1~$μ$s per packet.

title: Device-Centric Cooperative Floor-Level Estimation under Sparse Anchor Deployment for Construction-Site Applications
summary: For construction-site applications in multi-story buildings, accurate floor-level estimation is important for tracking workers, equipment, and Internet of Things (IoT) devices. In buildings under construction, communication infrastructure and power-supply facilities are often limited and the indoor environment changes as construction progresses, making localization systems that rely on dense wireless infrastructure or fingerprint databases difficult to deploy and maintain. Low-power wide-area (LPWA) communication can provide wide-area coverage with a small number of temporarily deployed access points (APs), but under sparse AP deployment, AP-to-terminal observations alone may provide insufficient floor-related information for reliable floor-level estimation. To address this problem, this paper develops a device-centric cooperative floor-level estimation method that exploits inter-terminal observations as relative floor-difference information to complement AP-side information. For practical application with limited measurement data, AP-to-terminal observations are represented by an upper/lower-AP RSS contrast, while inter-terminal observations are statistically modeled according to floor-difference classes. The resulting AP-side and pairwise scores are combined in a weighted floor-label objective and approximately optimized using dual-order sequential iterated conditional modes (ICM). Ray-tracing simulations and LoRa measurement experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method under different AP deployments and terminal-selection limits.

title: Watermark Evidence under Open-Weight LLM Modification: Exact Bounds for Low-Rank Output Watermarks
summary: Open-weight language models can continue generating after their released weights are modified, while a watermark verifier still scores outputs against the original base and marked models. We study how such modifications change the evidence available to an OpenStamp-style verifier. At each shared prefix, we represent the modification as a residual in the next-token logits. We derive an exact finite-vocabulary lower bound on the expected log-likelihood-ratio evidence under a residual-span constraint, along with a sharp span-only deviation bound. We also characterize the first-order evidence shift through a covariance term with an explicit second-order remainder, and determine the residual span needed to reach a target evidence level. For sequence-level detection, we derive an exact conditional exponential-moment bound and combine it with a supermartingale argument and a distribution-free order-statistic tolerance bound. This yields a high-confidence upper bound on miss probability after attack selection on calibration data and evaluation on independent certification continuations. In experiments with OpenStamp on Llama-2-7B and Mistral-7B-v0.3, INT8 quantization and 30% pruning retain test true-positive rates of 85.6-94.8%, while 500-step LoRA fine-tuning lowers them to 28.8% and 11.6%. The covariance prediction tracks the measured mean LoRA evidence drift on both models, with no remainder-bound violations across 160,000 test prefixes. Additionally, we observe zero false positives among 500 base-model continuations per model. Through these theoretical and empirical results, the current research provides a better understanding of watermark robustness to model-editing/tuning attacks.

title: TIBECG: Temporal Information Bottleneck for Lead-Specific Demographic Privacy in ECG Waveform Release
comment: 12 pages, 9 figures, 2 tables. Corresponding author: Tsai-Min Chen
summary: Transmitting an electrocardiogram (ECG) waveform can expose demographic information beyond an intended diagnostic task. We evaluate TIBECG, an architectural temporal information bottleneck, on individual leads extracted from hospital twelve-lead recordings. A 2,302,337-parameter processor varies its latent length while retaining the same nine-score consistency objective, without age or sex labels in protector fitting. Across 6,386 recordings, ten folds, 12 leads and 21 lengths, retrospective selections retained at least 95% of each lead's clean macro-F1. Their weaker age/sex interval gain exceeded the best eligible conventional transformation on all leads, by a median 22.08 percentage points. The implemented sampling-rate comparison shows that direct downsampling usually suppresses demographic inference more strongly but at a larger loss of diagnostic utility, whereas TIBECG favors utility preservation. Selection stability also varies by lead. Lower latent Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence does not reliably rank residual sex leakage at a fixed length. These findings support lead-specific evaluation of waveform processing, not validated consumer deployment or expert-readable reconstruction. When the waveform-input diagnostic classifier is hosted as part of a proprietary cloud service rather than deployed on the device, waveform transmission is required to obtain its scores.

title: Tie-Line Scheduling Using Real-Time Contraction Metrics: Hierarchical Reachable Sets for Multi-Area Inverter-Dominated Grids
summary: Managing transmission congestion in multi-area power grids dominated by inverter-based resources (IBRs) requires bridging a severe timescale and modeling divide. Supervisory congestion optimizers -- such as Online Feedback Optimization (OFO) and two-tiered differentiable Model Predictive Control (MPC) -- rely on linearized, convex algebraic grid approximations that cannot guarantee dynamic stability during sub-second converter transients. Conversely, fast distributed consensus schemes like Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) depend on convex plant assumptions and iterative message exchanges that lag behind rapid tie-line surges. This paper replaces convex ADMM emergency consensus with a Distributed Nonlinear Separable Control Contraction Metric (SCCM) architecture spanning three nested tiers: the Device layer, the Area layer, and the Grid tie-line layer. By pairing online Prediction Error Method and Moving Horizon Estimation (PEM-MHE) parameter tracking with offline convex Linear Matrix Inequality (LMI) synthesis, the controller executes a closed-form nonlinear feedback law online without solving real-time optimization problems. We derive the Pontryagin attainable (reachable) ellipsoids for each layer, prove hierarchical tube containment via Schur-complement matrix inequalities, and project the certified Grid reachable tube through Power Transfer Distribution Factors (PTDFs) to supply guaranteed safe thermal limits to the supervisory coordinator. Validation on modified IEEE 39-bus (100% IBR, zero synchronous generators) and 3-area IEEE 118-bus systems demonstrates an 82.8% reduction in cumulative tie-line thermal overload while maintaining strict exponential contraction ($λ_{\max} \le -2.43$) even under a 3 s communication blackout.

title: Constructions of reversible linear and DNA codes through $T_{D,g}^n-$set and $(n_1,c_1|n_2,c_2)-$right polycyclic codes
summary:
In this paper we give a construction technique of $T_{D,g}^n-$set for reversible linear codes and reversible DNA codes with their code parameters. This technique yields many reversible MDS codes which significantly improves the $T^n-$set construction by Oztas et.al. in terms of obtained code parameters. Concatenation-based constructions are presented for reversible linear codes satisfying self-duality and linear complementary dual (LCD) conditions, giving necessary and sufficient condition for desired dual properties.
  We introduce a new notion of $(n_1,c_1|n_2,c_2)-$ right polycyclic codes. Also, a new construction technique is developed to obtain reversible linear $(n_1,c_1|n_2,c_2)-$ right polycyclic codes with good parameters (MDS codes) over any finite commutative rings.

title: Do LLMs Understand Network Traces? A Comparative Study of Reasoning over Raw and Filtered Traffic Data
comment: This publication has been submitted to NOMS2027
summary: The effective delivery and monitoring of ICT services rely heavily on network traffic analysis. However, interpreting complex packet captures remains a challenging task that requires substantial technical expertise. Large language models (LLMs) offer promising opportunities to automate network traffic in- vestigation, yet their reliability in packet-level field extraction and flow-level sequence reconstruction remains an open research question. This study proposes a reproducible, question-answering- based evaluation methodology to assess the capabilities of LLMs in network trace analysis. Using real-world benign traffic from the CICIDS2017 dataset, we evaluate multiple models against a human-generated ground truth, comparing their performance on raw textual traffic dumps and protocol-filtered representations. Model responses are assessed through an automated LLM- as-a-judge pipeline, validated against human evaluations. The results demonstrate that protocol filtering significantly reduces prompt overhead while improving answer accuracy by reducing incorrect responses. These findings highlight the importance of protocol-aware traffic filtering as an effective optimization for improving the efficiency and reliability of LLM-assisted network management.

title: Hardware Impairment Parameter Estimation in Fluid Antenna Systems by Inverse Optimization
summary: In this paper, the problem of estimating the hardware impairment parameters of fluid antennas (FAs) in a multi-base station (BS) multi-user communication system is studied. The actual hardware coefficients are unknown, whereas the FA positions and transmit beamforming vectors adopted by the BSs are known. We first formulate a forward spectral efficiency (SE) maximization problem and introduce aggregate interference variables whose consistency with the physical inter-cell interference can be maintained through a pricing mechanism. For inverse estimation, the aggregate interference is obtained from receiver-side interference measurements associated with the observed network decisions. We then construct a trust-region linear model of the position-update problem around the observed FA positions. To extend the applicability of the proposed framework to antenna positions obtained from inexact or heuristic algorithms, we develop an inverse optimization model with an explicit duality-gap tolerance, which is solved using sequential quadratic programming (SQP). Simulation results show that the proposed scheme attains a lower estimation error than KKT residual minimization (KKT-RM) at both considered transmit-power levels and improves the SE by up to 22.86% over the Ideal-hardware-assumption scheme.

title: LLMs as Validators for Cross-Chain Bridges: Evaluating Source-Level and Transaction-Level Attack Detection on Solana
summary: Cross-chain bridges have suffered substantial asset losses due to vulnerabilities in their on-chain programs. On Solana, missing validation checks can enable exploits even when the underlying blockchain operates correctly. The ability of large language models (LLMs) to diagnose these flaws from source code or transaction records, rather than merely raise alarms, remains insufficiently understood. We implement a native Rust lock-and-mint bridge on a local Solana validator with four exploitable variants: two model flaws from the Cashio and Wormhole incidents, while the other two represent vulnerability classes documented in Solana security audits. Paired vulnerable and secure programs, together with successful attacks, benign sessions, and blocked attempts, allow us to distinguish correct diagnoses from unsupported alarms. We evaluate six configurations of five open-weight models across 16,800 responses, compare source inputs with and without comments, and grade 7,200 answers on vulnerable inputs using two blinded LLM graders. The results reveal substantial differences across conditions: without comments, models diagnose 24% of vulnerable source inputs while frequently flagging the secure bridge. Transaction diagnosis is high for the missing-signer scenario but averages 6% across the other three scenarios. Original comments, some of which describe the flaw, increase source diagnosis to 60%. These findings highlight the importance of distinguishing correct vulnerability diagnoses from unsupported alarms in bridge security review.

title: Layerwise Learning-Rate Scaling in Vision Networks: Effective-Rate Identification, Power-Mean Aggregation, and Budget Dependence
comment: 10 pages, 6 figures. Supplementary material (15 pages) included as an ancillary file. Data and analysis scripts: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24279433
summary: Layerwise learning-rate scaling assigns different learning rates to different parts of a network. Although established in fine-tuning pretrained models, its effects in vision networks trained from scratch are commonly assessed by training each candidate recipe. We show that, in this setting, the rate-related component of a layerwise strategy is well summarized by an effective learning rate computable directly from its multiplier profile. Across matched-control comparisons, changes in test accuracy closely track changes in training loss (r = -0.996), which supports an optimization-progress explanation of the short-budget rate effect. Increasing the untuned base learning rate tenfold shifts the rate-matched contrast upward in all six tested architectures (p = 0.016) and increases the number of architectures in which a published discriminative schedule, excluded from model fitting, outperforms the uniform control from two to five of six (p = 0.031). Within the evaluated strategy space, a parameter-weighted power mean with exponent 0.35 (95% confidence interval [0.20, 0.50]) accounts for 42.6% of within-architecture variance, compared with 36.4% for the arithmetic mean. Ranking candidates by this scalar without training improves the selected candidate's mean percentile rank from the 26th to the 10th and reduces its mean accuracy shortfall relative to the best candidate from 3.70 to 1.12 points. The rate-related effect decays as the training budget increases; relative to tuned baselines, the overall strategy effect falls within the prespecified practical-equivalence margin in two of three architectures. A separate grouping-related contrast can persist at long budgets, although its direction and magnitude depend on the architecture.

title: Who Gets the Grid Capacity? Allocating Dynamic Access Among Multiple Virtual Power Plants
summary: Virtual power plants (VPPs) trade in the same wholesale market and share distribution lines and transformers, and uncoordinated, profit-maximizing VPPs can push a shared transformer past its thermal limit or drive a feeder voltage out of band. The utility, which only observes the front-of-the-meter net injection at each bus, must keep the network safe from that net injection alone. We allocate a 24-hour active and reactive operating envelope to each VPP by a Benders decomposition: the utility sets a trial envelope, each VPP solves its private convex portfolio problem, and the returned value and dual gradient become supporting cuts that rebuild its value function while its schedule, state, and cost stay private. The envelope carries the transformer's thermal state across hours, bounds a joint conditional value-at-risk over forecast uncertainty, and is re-optimized each hour with the current hour committed. On a reduced IEEE-13 feeder with real load and prices, an active-power-only implementation lowers the transformer's peak-temperature CVaR from 254 to 97\,$^\circ$C at a 28\% value give-up and holds the transformer below its limit where nameplate access breaches it.

title: Hardness and Inapproximability of the Covering Radius for LDPC Codes
summary: Given a binary parity-check matrix $H$ and an integer $r$, the covering-radius decision problem asks whether every attainable syndrome can be represented by an error vector of Hamming weight at most $r$. We study this problem for sparse parity-check matrices with bounded row and column weights. Using a bounded-occurrence quantified-SAT reduction, we prove that the problem is $Π_2^{\mathrm P}$-complete for matrices with maximum row and column weight three, and remains $Π_2^{\mathrm P}$-hard under a constant multiplicative gap. Starting from Vertex Cover on 3-regular graphs, we also obtain an explicit NP-hard approximation factor under the same weight constraints. We remark that weight three is the exact threshold for hardness: if either the maximum row weight or the maximum column weight is at most two, the covering radius can be computed in polynomial time.

title: Gateway-Free Kafka Streaming from FPGA-Based Detectors: A Bare-Metal Pipelined Producer on Zynq-7000
comment: Accepted for pucblishing at IEEE Explore proceedings of ARGENCON 2026
summary:
We present a bare-metal Apache Kafka producer implemented on a Zynq-7000 System-on-Chip (SoC) for event-driven data acquisition. Events are generated in Programmable Logic (PL), transferred to the Processing System (PS) through AXI4-Stream and AXI DMA, and published to a standard Kafka broker without an intermediate gateway computer. The PS constructs ProduceRequest messages and transmits them through the lwIP raw TCP/IP API. A configurable pipeline limits the number of outstanding Kafka requests.
  Pipeline depths of D = 1, 2, 4, and 8 were evaluated with two independent DMA sources. For each depth, 20 independent runs of 5,000 events were acquired, for 400,000 event records in total. Each event carries a 32-bit frame counter and a 32-bit PL timestamp. PS-side instrumentation records DMA start and completion, publication, successful local tcp_write() acceptance, and reception of the corresponding Kafka acknowledgement. Measurement records are exported to a separate Kafka topic after the timed event stream has completed.
  Each of the 80 runs contained 5,000 records with frame values from 0 to 4,999, with no sequence discontinuities in the exported metric records and no recorded Kafka errors. Mean operational throughput was approximately 5.3 kevents/s at D = 1, 9.4-9.6 kevents/s at D = 2, 16.2 kevents/s at D = 4, and 16.8-17.5 kevents/s at D = 8. The median publish-to-acknowledgement interval was 1.62-1.64 ms at D = 1, 0.98 ms at D = 2, 0.66 ms at D = 4, and 0.83-0.86 ms at D = 8. At D = 4, the corresponding P95 values were 0.81-0.83 ms.

title: Edge-Combining Subharmonic Mixer-First Receiver
summary: A 1-10 GHz subharmonic mixer-first receiver using edge combining to drive N-path switches from 50% duty-cycle clocks at half the local oscillator (LO) frequency avoids the gain penalty of harmonic mixing. Inverter-based differential baseband amplifiers with back-gate feedback linearization set their gain by process-defined capacitance ratios, using no additional components and consuming no additional power. A 22 nm fully depleted silicon on insulator (FD-SOI) prototype receiver achieves a conversion gain of 12.8-18.1 dB and a noise figure of 5.7-11 dB across the band. It achieves up to 15.4 dBm out-of-band IIP3 while consuming 16.7-22.3 mW.

title: Threat Landscape of Vibe Coding and the Road to Secure Autonomy
comment: 35 pages, 6 figures, 5 tables, Submitted to ACM Computing Surveys
summary: Vibe coding is reshaping software development, enabling faster implementation and allowing individuals with limited programming experience to describe requirements in natural language while AI agents write, test, and deploy the code. As these agents evolve into autonomous systems that execute commands, manage dependencies, access cloud resources, and interact with other agents, their security risks extend beyond incorrect code to actions with direct consequences for software systems. Although research on these risks is expanding, it remains fragmented across areas including prompt injection, insecure code generation, supply-chain attacks, and human factors, with limited consensus on terminology, threat assumptions, and evaluation. This paper consolidates emerging research through the lens of the vibe coding workflow. We establish a reference architecture, characterise six levels of agent autonomy, and develop a threat model centred on five trust boundaries spanning developers, AI models, tools, cloud infrastructure, and the wider software ecosystem. Building on this foundation, we propose a taxonomy of twenty-one threats across nine classes. For each threat, we review the available evidence, assess proposed defences, and identify limitations. Our analysis highlights that risks increase with agents' operational authority, while most defences rely on model judgement and address isolated threats. Finally, we identify eleven research challenges, including enforceable limits on agent authority and shared benchmarks and methodologies for assessing vibe coding security.

title: FACE: Flow-Guided Angular Channel Estimation Framework for mmWave MIMO Systems
summary: Acquiring accurate channel state information (CSI) is essential for millimeter-wave (mmWave) multi-input multi-output (MIMO) systems. However, it remains challenging due to high-dimensional channels, limited pilot observations, and measurement noise. To address these challenges, we propose flow-guided angular channel estimation (FACE), a novel channel estimation framework based on flow matching, an emerging generative modeling paradigm that learns continuous transport dynamics between probability distributions. FACE exploits the inherent angular-domain sparsity of mmWave channels and incorporates the learned flow matching model as a generative channel prior. Numerical results show that FACE consistently achieves higher channel estimation accuracy than both conventional estimators and diffusion-based generative estimator across diverse channel and system configurations. Moreover, FACE maintains high estimation accuracy with fewer pilot observations and achieves an average achievable rate close to the perfect-CSI benchmark. Compared with diffusion-based estimation, FACE requires substantially fewer sampling steps while achieving superior or comparable estimation accuracy, reducing inference time and computational cost. Overall, the proposed framework demonstrates the potential of flow matching for accurate, pilot-efficient, and computationally efficient mmWave MIMO channel estimation.

title: Emerging Vertical Power Delivery in AI Data Centers: Challenges and Solutions
comment: 29 pages, 24 figures. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible
summary: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) workloads is increasing power demand in AI data centers, and processor current is projected to reach 2000 A and beyond. This trend is exposing the limitations of lateral power delivery (LPD) to processors and has motivated growing interest in vertical power delivery (VPD). This paper reviews the power delivery network (PDN) of AI data centers and the upcoming transition from LPD to VPD. First, the 800 VDC power delivery architecture, the impedance behavior of the PDN, and the limitations of LPD are discussed. Then, VPD implementation approaches, reported converter designs, and packaging technologies are examined, together with integrated voltage regulators (IVRs) and embedded passive components. In addition, power integrity simulations are presented to compare regulator and plane positions, from which a set of PDN design guidelines is derived. The results show that moving a voltage regulator module (VRM) from 50 mm away to directly below the die reduces the loop inductance by nearly half. In a complete PDN, this relocation lowers the low-frequency anti-resonant peak, whereas the mid- and high-frequency impedance depends on the decoupling stages and the position of the power and ground planes. This paper also shows that achieving practical VPD remains closely tied to challenges such as regulator height, passive-component embedding, and thermal management.

title: Optimal Min-Entropy Estimation with High Probability
summary: Min-entropy plays a fundamental role in assessing the unpredictability of randomness sources. In particular, NIST SP 800-90B specifies min-entropy estimation as a key procedure for entropy sources used in cryptographic random bit generators, illustrating the practical importance of reliable min-entropy estimation. In this paper, we settle the sample complexity of min-entropy estimation with high probability in both the classical and quantum cases. Specifically, for min-entropy estimation with additive error $\varepsilon$ and probability at least $1-δ$, the sample complexity is $Θ(d\log(d/δ)/\varepsilon^2)$ for classical distributions on $d$ symbols and $Θ((d^2+d\log(1/δ))/\varepsilon^2)$ for quantum states on a $d$-dimensional Hilbert space. Our results admit short and simple proofs.

title: Temporal Diffusion Models for Joint Signal-Channel Estimation under Gaussian and $α$-Stable MIMO Channels
summary: Diffusion models have emerged as powerful tools for learning complex data distributions and solving inverse problems. However, most diffusion models rely on the Gaussian distribution, which does not accurately represent heavy-tailed data. In this work, we study diffusion-based reconstruction under Gaussian and symmetric $α$-stable fading channels, while also exploring the benefits of using possible temporal dependence in the channel. We consider two variants: pilot-based channel-only estimation and joint image-channel recovery for MIMO systems. Our approach is based on several standard and score-based diffusion models for both Gaussian and $α$-stable distributions. We refine these models by guiding the reverse diffusion process using the observation likelihood and show how a single trained diffusion model can be reused for the location-scale family of distributions without retraining. In blind MIMO recovery, separate diffusion models are used for the image and channel, and their estimates are combined through likelihood guidance. For each setting, we compare independent and temporal reconstruction, where information from previous observations is used to improve the estimation. We show that, under a time-dependent channel model, such a temporal reconstruction improves channel estimation and the quality of the reconstructed image. Finally, we show that, for the same heavy-tailed channel data, using an $α$-stable diffusion prior provides better channel estimation and image reconstruction than using a Gaussian diffusion prior.

title: Bajillion: Cryptographic Clearing for Micropayments
summary:
Much of the web is funded by advertising, a model that erodes as humans delegate browsing to AI agents acting on their behalf. A natural replacement is for agents to pay for what they consume, often a fraction of a cent per request. At the scale of web traffic, this could mean tens or even hundreds of millions of payments per second.
  We present Bajillion, a clearing protocol for scalable micropayments. A sender signs a payment request, and an untrusted operator answers with a preconfirmation, which promises the receiver that it will be paid. Periodically, the operator closes an epoch by posting only the net effect of its payments on chain. Bajillion guarantees that a malicious operator can only omit payments -- it can never debit a sender beyond what it signed, nor misdirect a transfer. Posted balances are therefore finalized immediately and can be withdrawn. By design, senders never have to raise disputes, making it suitable for ephemeral AI agents. A receiver that is shortchanged can prove that a close omitted a preconfirmed payment, which halts the protocol and lets every user exit with its finalized balance. Requests from different senders can be processed independently, allowing the operator to parallelize up to the number of senders. We capture these guarantees in an ideal functionality for accountable clearing and prove that Bajillion realizes it.

title: Hybrid Quantum Selection of Learning Rates in Language-Model Training: Termination Criteria and an Interaction-Guided Schedule Oracle
summary: Learning-rate choices strongly affect language-model fine-tuning, but the best joint profile across layer groups is generally unknown. This paper studies quantum minimum finding for layer-group learning-rate selection within a hybrid classical-quantum training framework. It combines Durr-Hoyer minimum finding with BBHT search and compares fixed-budget and confidence-based stopping policies using a lookup oracle built from measured profile scores at fixed training checkpoints. The paper then introduces an Interaction-Guided Schedule Oracle that scores and marks joint schedules in superposition without a precomputed score table. Classical one-step loss measurements supply the main, pairwise and three-way interaction effects between layer groups. The circuit adds the effects for each schedule, compares the resulting score with the current baseline score, and marks improving schedules for amplitude amplification. Measured candidates are checked classically before acceptance. Uniform-rate training supplies the initial baseline; using schedules from classical adaptive methods as baselines for joint refinement is left for future work. In closed-loop fine-tuning of a 1.5-billion-parameter language model, each selected schedule drives the next 200 classical training steps. Benchmark accuracies lie within the range observed across five uniform-rate seeds. The results give a working example of how quantum superposition can support adaptive learning-rate selection during training; the remaining quantum limitations are discussed in the paper.

title: First-Order Model-Free Policy Gradient for Undiscounted LQR with Global Optimality and Convergence Guarantees
summary: We provide a first-order model-free policy gradient (PG) framework for learning undiscounted infinite-horizon linear quadratic regulator (LQR) policies with global optimality and convergence guarantees. We first construct a stochastic wrapper policy class parameterized by the LQR gain to enable exploration around a deterministic linear control law. We analyze the additional cost induced by exploration over infinite-horizon, and establish a weak gradient dominance condition that characterizes global optimality under exploration. We then construct a model-free first-order PG algorithm using sampled trajectory information, without identifying the dynamics or approximating a value function. Finally, we establish finite-time convergence guarantees, providing the sufficient number of samples required for near-global optimality with our proposed PG algorithms.

title: Multi-connectivity in Wireless Access
summary: This paper investigates whether or not multi-connectivity, in which a User Equipment (UE) can simultaneously connect to multiple Access Points (APs), can offer a better Quality of Experience (QoE) to the users. Intuitively, multi-connectivity should offer a smoother bit rate (possibly at the expense of the average bit rate being slightly lower), so that adaptive applications can better determine at which throughput to send without introducing queueing latency. We mainly concentrate on how to share the resources of the APs amongst the UEs, modelling the lower layers via spectral efficiency and the higher layers via utility and its fluctuation. We explore various policies for resource allocation. Our results demonstrate that from the application point of view multi-connectivity is beneficial and show how to tune the parameters of the policies to obtain the best trade-off between average utility and its fluctuation.

title: Least ln-cosh-based adaptive filtering algorithm for graph signal processing
comment: Accepted for publication in IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
summary: Currently, an increasing number of irregular signals are being defined within graph structures. This paper proposes a Least ln-cosh-based Adaptive Filtering for Graph Signal Processing (GSP LLAF) algorithm for offline/online graph signal estimation under various non-Gaussian noise conditions. Compared to the recently proposed Graph Adaptive Least Mean p-th Power (GSP LMP) algorithm, GSP LLAF eliminates the need for prior knowledge of the noise characteristics. Simultaneously, GSP LLAF addresses the limitation in estimation accuracy encountered by the Sign Algorithm for Graph Signal Processing (GSP Sign) and the Graph Signal Processing algorithm based on the Generalized Maximum Correntropy Criterion (GSP GMCC). Furthermore, the algorithm features low computational complexity and fast execution speed. To achieve a balance between convergence speed and estimation accuracy, a variable step-size variant, the Modified Variable Step-Size Least ln-cosh-based Adaptive Filtering Algorithm for Graph Signal Processing (GSP MVSS-LLAF), is proposed. In estimation experiments involving both static and time-varying graph signals, the proposed GSP LLAF and GSP MVSS-LLAF algorithms demonstrate fast, stable, and robust graph signal estimation performance under various non-Gaussian noise conditions, including Bernoulli-Gaussian (BG) modeled impulse noise, as well as alpha-stable, Cauchy, and Laplace distributions.

title: A Forensic Analysis of Metadata and Information Leakage in Swedish Public Documents
summary: This study investigates metadata and structural content leakage in publicly available PDF documents from 30 Swedish public-sector authorities. Using an automated collection pipeline and ExifTool-based extraction, 2,876 documents were analyzed and classified using an R0-R3 risk taxonomy. Results reveal that 48.4% of documents exhibit significant metadata exposure (R2 or R3), with significant variation across institutional tiers (p < 0.001). Longitudinal analysis across three legislative periods reveals a statistically significant reduction in metadata exposure between the baseline and post-enactment periods, yet 44.9% of documents published after the enactment of the Swedish Cybersäkerhetslagen continue to leak sensitive metadata. Furthermore, 41.6% of documents contain incremental update layers; forensic analysis recovered verifiable text alterations, including deleted personal data and internal identifiers, from 228 of these cases. These findings highlight persistent regulatory lag and a systemic reliance on default, unsanitized document publication workflows within the Swedish public sector.

title: Margin Dynamics for Large Language Model Alignment
summary: Practitioners choose among LLM alignment methods largely by trial and error. We provide a theoretical foundation: each pairwise method defines a vector field on the probability simplex that governs how the model redistributes mass between preferred and dispreferred completions. Projecting onto a single preferred/dispreferred pair reduces this to a one-dimensional margin ODE with a closed-form solution. These solutions reveal that DPO margins grow without bound (logarithmically as $O(\log t)$ in the gradient-flow limit) while IPO margins converge to a finite $1/(2τ)$; that label noise induces a qualitative phase transition in DPO (unbounded $\to$ bounded) but affects IPO only quantitatively; and that gradient concentration under asymmetric weighting governs trainability at scale. We confirm all three predictions across five model families spanning four benchmarks. The closed-form solutions also enable principled method design: we prove that adding any label smoothing $\varepsilon > 0$ to SimPO creates a finite margin attractor at $Δ^* = β^{-1}\log((1-\varepsilon)/\varepsilon)$, while $\varepsilon = 0$ (standard SimPO) has no attractor. We test this across three models (8B-9B) and confirm the prediction: the theory-derived configuration (TPO-S, $\varepsilon = 0.05$) is competitive with the strongest baselines, attaining the highest mean IFEval score among the compared methods on all three, validating that the predicted finite attractor is a usable operating point rather than proposing a new state-of-the-art loss.

title: Safe Reinforcement Learning with Hard Constraints: Policy Gradient Methods with Intersample Guarantees
summary: We develop a policy-gradient (PG) reinforcement learning (RL) framework with hard inter-sample control barrier function (CBF)-based safety constraints for nonlinear sampled-data systems. We first design a class of stochastic policies with support truncated to sampling-period-dependent safe control sets, that guarantee safety-by-construction at sampling instants. We then propose a model-free PG algorithm that searches over the class of safe-by-design policies and establish sufficient conditions on sampling-period such that any action sampled from safe control sets remains safe throughout the sampling interval, providing inter-sample guarantees. We further establish finite-time convergence and sample complexity guarantees for the proposed PG algorithm and characterize its global optimality under gradient dominance. Finally, we illustrate inter-sample safety guarantees on a safe quadrotor navigation environment.

title: CULypso: A Clustered Federated Unlearning paradigm for Vehicular Ad-Hoc Networks
summary: Unlearning has emerged as an essential security and privacy-preserving solution in Machine Learning, enabling networks to support their clients' rights for data erasure, as mandated by data protection regulations. Introducing such a non-trivial task to an edge, highly mobile and time-sensitive vehicular network is an even greater, largely unexplored challenge. This article argues that a hierarchical Federated Unlearning approach could be aptly integrated into vehicular ad-hoc networks (VANETs), leveraging topology and movement to reduce communication, resource and time costs, while effectively forgetting a client's influence on the global model updates. In order to achieve this, we propose CULypso, an approximate, surgical, hierarchical unlearning algorithm tailored for clustered VANETs. Inspired by the nymph in Greek mythology, Calypso, whose name translates to 'she who conceals the knowledge', CULypso, with the capital letters referencing \textbf{C}lustered \textbf{U}n\textbf{L}earning, aims to achieve exactly what its name suggests: conceal, erase or forget in our case, knowledge it contains. Extensive experiments uphold the potency of our paradigm with it performing approximately 65\% better than FedEraser in terms of time, server storage load, and unlearning fidelity while utterly outperforming baseline full retraining.

title: Robust DOA Estimation for GNSS-like Signals Under Jamming: A Rotation-Enhanced SWN-MUSIC Approach
summary: In jamming environments, accurate direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation for Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS)-like signals using antenna arrays is crucial for spoofing detection and subsequent countermeasures. However, estimation accuracy strongly depends on the incident direction of the signal of interest (SOI) under a given jamming and array configuration, with severe errors occurring in certain directions---a phenomenon whose physical mechanisms remain unclear. To address this gap, we identify two types of geometric ill-conditions between the array manifold and the jamming subspace, clarifying that certain directions suffer from inherently unfavorable observation geometry, which cannot be overcome by algorithmic refinement alone. Motivated by this insight, we introduce a paradigm namely rotational diversity, which treats the array attitude as a controllable sensing resource to actively reconfigure the observation geometry, thereby providing complementary perspectives in which the problematic directions can be accurately estimated. To implement this paradigm, we develop a Rotation-Enhanced Spatial Whitening and Normalized Multiple Signal Classification (SWN-MUSIC) framework, which performs independent DOA estimations across multiple rotation angles and selectively integrates reliable estimates. Simulation results demonstrate substantial improvement in accuracy in the directions that were poorly estimated under the fixed-array SWN-MUSIC, while maintaining performance in well-conditioned directions, thereby producing more robust DOA estimates.

title: CNN Architecture Comparison for Malware Classification with Limited Training Data
summary: Traditional malware classification methods struggle to keep pace with rapidly evolving threats. Image-based malware classification offers a promising alternative by converting malware binaries into grayscale images for analysis with deep learning. While effective, organizations often face practical constraints in acquiring sufficient training data, especially for newer threats. This thesis investigates dual-path CNN architectures with intermediate feature fusion as a potential enhancement for malware classification, with particular focus on how varying training data size affects their comparative performance against traditional single-path approaches. This research implements and compares two models: a baseline single-path using the pre-trained VGG16 architecture and a dual-path model that combines VGG16 with a custom CNN through intermediate feature fusion. Both architectures are evaluated on a binary classification task distinguishing between two malware families (C2Lop.P trojan and Dialplatform.B worm) from the Malimg dataset. Each model is trained across four different training data proportions (20%, 40%, 60%, and 80%), with three training runs per size to ensure statistical robustness, while being evaluated on complementary test sets of varying sizes. Though both architectures achieved perfect classification performance across all training percentages, the study revealed significant differences in secondary metrics including training efficiency, robustness to noise perturbation, and architectural complexity. The findings challenge common assumptions about complex architectures, demonstrating that simpler models can offer superior efficiency and robustness without sacrificing classification performance in image-based malware analysis.

title: Learning Calibrated and Samplable Predictive Distributions of Surface-Ocean $Δp$CO$_2$ Using Tabular Diffusion Models
comment: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026). Workshop: Representations for the Physical Sciences
summary: The ocean absorbs almost 30% of anthropogenic CO$_2$ emissions, but quantifying this sink requires estimating surface-ocean CO$_2$ from observations that are sparse in space and time. Most existing machine-learning estimates of this field are deterministic, giving a single value per grid point, with uncertainty approximated post hoc via residuals, ensembles, or prescribed distributions. We instead learn a conditional predictive distribution for each observation: using Treeffuser, a conditional diffusion model with gradient-boosted-tree score functions, we estimate the full predictive distribution of $Δp$CO$_2$ (the sea-air $p$CO$_2$ difference) from 13 environmental, spatial, and temporal predictors. On a held-out SOCAT test set, Treeffuser attains the lowest continuous ranked probability score among the uncertainty-quantification methods evaluated (8.229 $μ$atm) and the coverage closest to the nominal 68% / 95% levels (0.686 / 0.930), while retaining point-prediction skill comparable to a deterministic XGBoost baseline (RMSE 18.4 vs. 17.7 $μ$atm; $R^2$ 0.77 vs. 0.79). These results show that conditional diffusion can provide well-calibrated, observation-level uncertainties while largely preserving point-prediction skill. Because Treeffuser is generative, its samples can support probabilistic analyses of $Δp$CO$_2$; extending this to spatially coherent field reconstruction will require modeling dependence across grid cells and evaluation on spatially held-out data.

title: PS-HalluBench: Taxonomy-Driven Benchmarking of LLM Hallucinations in Power Systems
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly explored for power-system applications, yet their reliability in engineering analysis remains uncertain. We introduce PS-HalluBench, a manually constructed benchmark of 200 questions that evaluates hallucination-related failures across five power-system task categories: numerical reasoning, network topology, constraint verification, false-premise acceptance, and abstention. We evaluate ten LLMs over the benchmark, yielding 39.35\% overall correctness, with constraint verification achieving only 21.75\%, and highlighting persistent difficulties in engineering reasoning. We further investigate engineering-grounded reasoning through numerical solver support and verified network information both of which show significant performance improvement. The findings reveal important limitations of standalone LLM reasoning and motivate integrating LLMs with verified engineering tools for reliable power-system analysis.

title: Reference Coordinates, Output Perturbations, and Information Loss in EEG Decoding
comment: 45 pages including supplementary material; 5 figures in the main text. Data and code included as ancillary material
summary: Electroencephalography (EEG) decoders can respond to reference changes that preserve all relative-potential information. We use established measurement-operator theory to distinguish coordinate sensitivity, additional output-channel perturbations, and electrode loss. Exact pseudoinverse alignment supplies a consistency control; measurement-operator canonicalization (MOC) denotes a graph-Tikhonov estimator. The broader evaluation covers three public motor-imagery datasets and four decoders. The primary EEGNet comparison on Cho2017 and PhysioNet uses three paired training seeds, three shared noise realizations, and six front ends, with identical CAR training inputs sharing checkpoints. At 10 dB output perturbation, MOC-minus-raw disagreement was -0.144 and -0.107, while balanced-accuracy differences were 0.044 and 0.050, respectively; these four contrasts passed the retained Holm correction. MOC also reduced disagreement relative to pseudoinversion across all three seeds in both cohorts. However, comparison with fixed graph smoothing after pseudoinversion did not establish an additional MOC benefit. Preserving zero reference rows changed raw disagreement by less than 0.001 in magnitude; inverse-method predictions were unchanged. For canonical front ends, cross-reference disagreement was close to the reference obtained from independent noise within the same operator. Controlled weak-mode reconstruction and equal-rank electrode masks exposed separate stability and information-loss effects. The results locate the complete-reference gains within spatial processing under the specified stress model, while requiring decoding accuracy alongside consistency to assess practical utility.

title: PersonaHate: A Scalable Persona-Based Data Synthesis Pipeline for Hate Speech Analysis
comment: 26 pages, 4 figures. Accepted at ACM CCS 2026
summary: Hate speech remains a persistent and evolving threat on online platforms. The widespread use of large language models (LLMs) further intensifies this problem by making hateful content easier and cheaper to generate at scale. Although stronger hate speech detectors continue to be proposed, their performance remains uneven across target identity groups and different forms of hateful expression, partly because existing training data provides only limited coverage of these cases. Thus, we introduce PersonaHate, a scalable persona-driven data synthesis pipeline for constructing diverse hate speech datasets. PersonaHate begins with a large persona pool of 457K personas drawn from two real-world sources. Conditioned on selected personas from this pool, it prompts eight LLMs to generate hate speech across 34 identity groups and performs multi-judge annotation to obtain reliable labels. The resulting corpus contains 791K samples, from which we curate a 67K group-balanced training set. Our modular design also supports extension to new identity groups, generators, and emerging hate targets. Built upon this dataset, we evaluate two detector training strategies: training from scratch and further fine-tuning. Results show that all trained models achieve competitive performance across four widely used external benchmarks. Notably, a 184M-parameter DeBERTa-v3 model trained on PersonaHate reaches 77.5% average F1 and 79.4% average accuracy, outperforming OpenAI's Moderation API on HateBenchSet and MHS. Furthermore, fine-tuning Llama-3.1-8B raises its average F1 from 70.7% to 78.4%, a gain of 7.7 percentage points, surpassing LlamaGuard-3, Meta's official safety model based on the same Llama-3.1-8B architecture, on three of four benchmarks. These results show that PersonaHate can substantially improve the robustness and cross-dataset generalization of hate speech detectors.

title: Regularized Score Centering
summary: Asynchronous reinforcement learning increases training throughput, but data from stale policies and numerical mismatch between training and inference can destabilize learning. To stabilize off-policy learning, score centering (SC) removes the effect of reward baselines on the expected update. Our gradient diagnostics show less extreme gradients with SC than with importance sampling (IS), but SC can still fail when the learner moves far from the behavior policy that generated the data. To limit this policy mismatch, we introduce Regularized Score Centering (RSC), which adds a reverse Kullback-Leibler (KL) penalty to encourage the learner's next-token distribution to stay close to the behavior policy's next-token distribution. RSC works with or without truncated importance sampling (TIS), which caps token importance weights. Our theoretical analysis supports this approach, showing that KL regularization improves convergence guarantees. We evaluate dense and mixture-of-experts models on mathematical reasoning and agentic tasks, including online shopping, tool use, games, and fully asynchronous software engineering. RSC with TIS substantially improves sample efficiency across all agentic benchmarks, attaining higher training rewards with the same number of sampled responses. In final evaluations, it achieves top performance across all six agentic tasks, improving by 14.3% on AppWorld and reaching 9.9 times the strongest baseline's score on BabyAI.

title: An Explainable Agentic AI Framework for Distribution System Load Restoration
summary: Distribution system load restoration is a sequential decision-making problem in which restoration actions must maximize served load, prioritize critical loads, and preserve power-flow feasibility. This paper proposes an explainable agentic artificial intelligence (AI) framework for distribution system load restoration. The proposed framework uses multiple large language model (LLM) agents for planner guidance, strategic plan generation, decision arbitration, memory-based feedback, and explanation generation. Unlike unconstrained LLM-based control, the proposed method restricts agent decisions to feasible restoration actions and evaluates all candidate plans using deterministic AC power-flow feasibility checks. The framework is evaluated on IEEE 33-bus and 69-bus distribution feeders, as well as a larger IEEE 118-bus test case, and compared against reinforcement learning and planning baselines. The results show that the proposed agentic framework achieves better restoration performance while producing structured explanations for operator-facing decision support. A direct comparison with a Single-LLM-Agent baseline further shows that the proposed multi-agent decomposition improves weighted restored load and critical-load recovery compared with a monolithic LLM decision structure.

title: Structured Design of Layered Sparse Unitary Space-Time Modulation for Integrated Noncoherent and Coherent MIMO Communications
summary: This work presents a novel structured constellation design based on unitary space-time modulation (USTM) for integrated noncoherent and coherent multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications. Information is encoded into the sparse space-time matrices through two layers: a noncoherent layer that distinguishes points on the Grassmann manifold (subspaces) and a coherent layer that distinguishes among the Stiefel representatives associated with each of those points (bases for the subspaces). We consider sequential decoding of the two layers to reduce computational complexity, while explicitly identifying the matrix structures that favor this decoding strategy. The proposed constellation builds on a previous structured Grassmannian signaling design, which has the remarkable property of producing space-time matrices with a single nonzero entry per row, while introducing a novel systematic design for the second layer corresponding to the Stiefel representatives. The design of the second layer preserves the sparsity of the first layer and significantly reduces the decoding computational complexity, while ensuring reliable performance under sequential decoding and enabling a simple yet effective bit labeling, as validated by numerical results in terms of bit error rate (BER) and symbol error rate (SER).
